links.outcome: AI DR detection performance on non-mydriatic vs mydriatic handheld images
links.effect: Accuracy 85.15% (AUC 0.94) mydriatic vs 79.68% (AUC 0.93) non-mydriatic; sensitivity difference significant (p=0.0001), AUC difference not significant (p=0.4666).
links.quote: The McNemar test showed a significant difference in sensitivity (p=0.0001), whereas DeLong's test revealed no significant difference in area under the curve (p=0.4666).

links.outcome: Optimal classification thresholds by mydriasis status
links.effect: Youden index optimal thresholds differed between mydriatic and non-mydriatic images, implying a single threshold is unsuited across acquisition conditions.
links.quote: The Youden index indicated that optimal classification thresholds differed based on mydriasis status.

links.outcome: AI diabetic retinopathy detection performance under mydriatic versus non-mydriatic image acquisition
links.effect: Accuracy was 85.15% with mydriasis versus 79.68% without; area under the curve was 0.94 versus 0.93. Sensitivity differed (p=0.0001), whereas area under the curve did not (p=0.4666).
links.quote: The AI model achieved better performance in mydriatic images (accuracy, 85.15%; area under the curve, 0.94) than in non-mydriatic images (accuracy, 79.68%; area under the curve, 0.93).
